name: Ogee-de-Luxe face massager

lead: The Ogee-de-Luxe is a vintage face massager dated to about 1920, made by Osborne Garratt and Co. and catalogued by the Science Museum Group among its domestic appliances. It belongs to the early twentieth-century wave of hand-operated beauty devices that people used at home to massage the face.

The appeal of such devices is the familiar one: massaging the face is said by users to freshen the complexion and ease the look of tiredness. The museum record identifies the object and its maker but gives no written account of its construction or reported results.

paras: Hand-held facial massagers of this era were generally moved over the face by the user as part of a home beauty routine. The museum entry does not describe how this particular model was operated.

Devices like it show how facial massage for a smoother, fresher-looking face was already a home-beauty pursuit a century ago. The museum's record consists of a photograph and catalogue details; it does not give a written description, materials or usage notes. [1]
